I don't have today's price move data for MPC, so I can't tell you whether the stock went up or down. However, the refining environment and recent news paint a mixed picture for a major oil refiner like Marathon Petroleum.

On the positive side, US refineries are running at 94.5 percent capacity—near peak utilization—which supports strong margins. But crude oil prices have weakened sharply: Brent crude has dipped below $90 for the first time since August on hopes that the Iran conflict may end "fairly soon," according to statements from President Trump. Lower oil prices typically squeeze refiner profit margins, even though high utilization rates help offset some of that pressure.

The political backdrop adds noise rather than clear direction. While a midterm election favored renewable energy over fossil fuels, diplomatic negotiations on Iran remain described as "unproductive" by Secretary of State Rubio—so the actual timing and likelihood of a real peace deal remains uncertain. Oil storage levels are solid and not signaling oversupply stress, so the weakness in crude prices reflects geopolitical sentiment more than fundamentals.
